## Instruction

The midterm has two components: the Rmarkdown notebook (html) and the presentation.  We will do the presentation in class. Post both the notebook and the presentation on your Github page. 

**The notebook:** The notebook should be created using `rmarkdown` or Quarto (like other assignments). The notebook should have a title. 


**The Presentation:** Present your results in 5-10 minutes. To make the presentation using Rmarkdown, do the follows: 

    - In Rstudio -> File -> New File -> R markdown
    
    - In the left panel, click to Presentation -> Click OK
    
    - Now you have an Rmarkdown that can be knitted to be a html presentation 
    
- You can also use the Rmd templates of the class slides. 

- You can also use Quarto to create the presentation: *In Rstudio -> File -> New File -> Quarto Presentation...*
    
- You do not need to rerun all the codes for the presentation. For example, to show the model comparison, you just need to show the image of the model comparison instead of running all the models again.
    
- To inset an image in a slide, use  `![](image.png)`

- To scale images, you can use `![](image.png){width="60%"}` or follow these below instructions. 
    
    - https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/figure-size.html
    
    - http://zevross.com/blog/2017/06/19/tips-and-tricks-for-working-with-images-and-figures-in-r-markdown-documents/

- To turn off message and warning of a code cell, use:  `{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}` for the cell. 

**What to present**:

  - Present Part 2 - Visualization
  
  - Present Question Question 4, 5 and 6 in Part 3.  
  
  - Present any errors/challenges you run into and how you fix/overcome them. 

**Data:**  

The data for the mid-term project is the Rhode Island Department of Health Hospital Discharge Data.  Each row of the data presents a patient. 

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=15QNBf6YYKocK2nNIfpKDer58kQnCPNZJ

- Since this is a large dataset, you could try to run the codes on the smaller dataset, which is a portion of the original dataset before running the codes on the original data.  To create a random subset of the data you could use

8. Which month admitted the most number of patients? Which month admitted the most number of male patients?

```{r}
  count(moa) %>%
```


15. Create a season (Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter) variable. Calculate the length of stays by season.  Which season has the longest length of stays on average?
```{r}
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    season = case_when(
      moa %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
      moa %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Spring",
      moa %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Summer",
      moa %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall"))

df %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(avg_los = mean(los, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_los))
```



16. On average, how much a 20 year-old male get charged for staying 1 day in the Fall season?
```{r}
df %>%
  filter(sex == "1", age == 20, los == 1, season == "Fall") %>%
  summarise(avg_charge = mean(total, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## III. Predictive Models

Continue with the data from part I. Make sure you do not have any missing values in the data. Use the follows as the target and input variables: 

*Target Variable*: Create the target variable taking value of 

  - `low` if the total charge of a patient (`tot`) is smaller than the median of the total charge, and

  - `high` otherwise. 

*Input Variables*:

  - "age","sex","raceethn","provider","moa","mod","admtype","campus", 'los'
  
-------

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Remove rows with missing values in relevant variables
df_model <- df %>%
  select(tot, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, mod,
         admtype, campus, los) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(
    charge_level = ifelse(
      tot < median(tot),
      "low",
      "high"
    ),
    charge_level = factor(charge_level)
  )
```


1. Use `filter` function to filter out rows where `raceethn==''` or `admtype==''`. Make sure all the categorical variables are factor, numeric variables are numeric. Set Training : Testing Split = 10 : 90 

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(caret)

# Filter rows and keep required variables
df_model <- df %>%
  select(tot, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, mod,
         admtype, campus, los) %>%
  filter(raceethn != "", admtype != "") %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(
    charge_level = ifelse(tot < median(tot), "low", "high"),
    charge_level = factor(charge_level),

    # categorical variables as factors
    sex = factor(sex),
    raceethn = factor(raceethn),
    provider = factor(provider),
    moa = factor(moa),
    mod = factor(mod),
    admtype = factor(admtype),
    campus = factor(campus),

    # numeric variables as numeric
    age = as.numeric(age),
    los = as.numeric(los)
  )

# 10% training, 90% testing
set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(
  df_model$charge_level,
  p = 0.10,
  list = FALSE
)

train_data <- df_model[train_index, ]
test_data  <- df_model[-train_index, ]

```


2. Train a decision tree using `rpart`.  Plot the decision tree. Plot the variable importance ranked by the tree. 

```{r}
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)

# Train decision tree
tree_model <- rpart(
  charge_level ~ age + sex + raceethn + provider +
    moa + mod + admtype + campus + los,
  data = train_data,
  method = "class"
)

# Plot decision tree
rpart.plot(
  tree_model,
  type = 2,
  extra = 104,
  fallen.leaves = TRUE,
  main = "Decision Tree for Charge Level"
)

# Variable importance
importance <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(tree_model$variable.importance),
  Importance = tree_model$variable.importance
)

# Sort by importance
importance <- importance[order(-importance$Importance), ]

#Plotting the importance to look at results 
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(importance,
       aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance),
           y = Importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Variable Importance from Decision Tree",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```



3. Using caret for this question. Set `Training Control` to be: Use Cross-Validation of 5 folds across all models.  Train & tune at least 2 different models (i.e. two different values for `method=` in the train function of caret).  Plot the hyper-parameter tuning plots for each model. 

```{r}
library(caret)

# 5-fold Cross Validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5
)

set.seed(123)

tree_fit <- train(
  charge_level ~ age + sex + raceethn + provider +
    moa + mod + admtype + campus + los,
  data = train_data,
  method = "rpart",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneLength = 10
)

knn_fit <- train(
  charge_level ~ age + sex + raceethn + provider +
    moa + mod + admtype + campus + los,
  data = train_data,
  method = "knn",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneLength = 10
)

plot(tree_fit)
plot(knn_fit)

```


4. Plot the comparison of the models in 3. 

```{r}
# Compare the models
results <- resamples(
  list(
    DecisionTree = tree_fit,
    KNN = knn_fit
  )
)

# Summary of performance
summary(results)


bwplot(results)
```


5. What is your final selection for the model? Test the accuracy of your final model on the test data. 

```{r}
# Determine best model
tree_acc <- max(tree_fit$results$Accuracy)
knn_acc  <- max(knn_fit$results$Accuracy)

if (tree_acc > knn_acc) {
  final_model <- tree_fit
  model_name <- "Decision Tree"
} else {
  final_model <- knn_fit
  model_name <- "KNN"
}

# Test performance
pred <- predict(final_model, test_data)

conf_mat <- confusionMatrix(pred, test_data$charge_level)

model_name
conf_mat$overall["Accuracy"]
```


6. Create another `target` variable (binary), decide the input variables and redo 1 to 5.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(caret)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(ggplot2)

# Create new dataset and target variable
df2 <- df %>%
  filter(raceethn != "", admtype != "") %>%
  select(los, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, mod,
         admtype, campus) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(
    los_level = ifelse(los < median(los), "short", "long"),
    los_level = factor(los_level),

    sex = factor(sex),
    raceethn = factor(raceethn),
    provider = factor(provider),
    moa = factor(moa),
    mod = factor(mod),
    admtype = factor(admtype),
    campus = factor(campus),

    age = as.numeric(age)
  )

# 10% Train / 90% Test Split
set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(
  df2$los_level,
  p = 0.10,
  list = FALSE
)

train_data <- df2[train_index, ]
test_data <- df2[-train_index, ]

# 5-Fold Cross Validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5
)

# Model 1: Decision Tree
tree_fit <- train(
  los_level ~ age + sex + raceethn + provider +
    moa + mod + admtype + campus,
  data = train_data,
  method = "rpart",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneLength = 10
)

# Plot Decision Tree
rpart.plot(tree_fit$finalModel)

# Variable Importance
importance <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(tree_fit$finalModel$variable.importance),
  Importance = tree_fit$finalModel$variable.importance
)

importance <- importance[order(-importance$Importance), ]

ggplot(importance,
       aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance),
           y = Importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Variable Importance for LOS Level Prediction",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Model 2: KNN
knn_fit <- train(
  los_level ~ age + sex + raceethn + provider +
    moa + mod + admtype + campus,
  data = train_data,
  method = "knn",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneLength = 10
)

# Hyperparameter Tuning Plots
plot(tree_fit)
plot(knn_fit)

# Compare the models
results <- resamples(
  list(
    DecisionTree = tree_fit,
    KNN = knn_fit
  )
)

# Summary of performance
summary(results)

# Visual comparison
bwplot(results)
dotplot(results)

# Select Best Model Using Accuracy
tree_acc <- max(tree_fit$results$Accuracy)
knn_acc <- max(knn_fit$results$Accuracy)

if (tree_acc > knn_acc) {
  final_model <- tree_fit
  model_name <- "Decision Tree"
} else {
  final_model <- knn_fit
  model_name <- "KNN"
}

cat("Selected Model:", model_name, "\n")

# Test Set Evaluation
pred <- predict(final_model, newdata = test_data)

conf_mat <- confusionMatrix(
  pred,
  test_data$los_level
)

print(conf_mat)

cat(
  "Test Accuracy:",
  round(conf_mat$overall["Accuracy"] * 100, 2),
  "%\n"
)
```


7. Write a paragraph to summarize the section and give your comments on the results. 

```{r}
# Predictive modeling is first classifying patients into two groups. First, a target variable based on total charges was created, where patients were labeled as either high or low charge depending on whether their total charge exceeded the median value. The data was then cleaned by converting categorical variables into factors, numeric variables were converted to numeric format, and the dataset was split into training and testing sets. A decision tree model was developed and used to identify the most important predictors of patient charges. I then created two models, Decision Tree and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), then trained and tuned using 5-fold cross-validation. Their performances were compared using accuracy, and the best-performing model was selected and evaluated on the test dataset. Finally, the process was repeated using a new target variable based on length of stay, classifying patients into short-stay and long-stay groups. The results demonstrated that patient charcteristics like age, admission information, and provider-related variables can be useful for predicting healthcare outcomes, while model comparison helped identify the most effective predictive approach for the dataset.
```
